messages:
Maria: Quick thread — seeing a 15–40% tail-latency regression on private smallgpu when continuous-batcher hits token_budget cap. Profiling + logs below. Anyone seen kernel selection flip and extra memcpy stalls during long KV reads?

Maria: Profiling summary (snip):
```
99th: 412ms -> 520ms
p99.9: 780ms -> 1120ms
throughput per GPU: -6% at peak
hot path: kernel_selector -> fallback to 'mem-optimized' path, plus bson-kv memcpy spikes
kv cache hit rate: 86% -> 72% during regressed window
```

Maria: Current private knobs: `batch_token_target=48`, `max_batch_wait_ms=12`, `kv_prefetch=false`, `kernel_pref=auto`.

Jon: Did this start after the kernel-selector change last week (commit f2d3a1)? Can repro locally if I force token streams to exceed budget.

Sasha: Looks like two interacting things: (1) token_budget cap triggers more frequent small flushes so kernel selection sees shorter seqs and picks different kernels, (2) KV read misses cause a memcpy stall that magnifies the tail. On smallgpus with constrained VRAM, the mempaths are fragile.

Kevin: Ran a quick micro-benchmark toggling batch token targets. Results (30k requests):
```
batch_token_target=48 -> p99 510ms
batch_token_target=64 -> p99 460ms
batch_token_target=32 -> p99 600ms
```
Throughput slightly down at 64 (~-3%) but tail improved.

Irene: grafana alert triggered: https://grafana/internal/d/ai/private-tail-latency?orgId=1 (spike window 03:12–03:24 UTC). CC perf team. :rotating_light:

perf-bot: Regression alert: private-smallgpu / tail-latency increased by 35% vs baseline. Auto-tagging: kernel-fallback, kv-misses.

Maria: Proposal for immediate mitigation (private-only config override):
```
batch_token_target: 64
max_batch_wait_ms: 8
kernel_selection_preference: memory-bound
kv_prefetch: true
```
This should bias toward slightly larger batches and prefetch KV to avoid memcpy stalls. Will accept small throughput hit.

Jon: I can run a 5% canary in eu-central on smallgpu tonight. Script to deploy tweak: 
```
./infra/deploy_canary.sh --env=private-eu --percent=5 --config-overrides="batch_token_target=64,max_batch_wait_ms=8,kv_prefetch=true"
```
I'll capture p50/p99/p99.9 and cost delta.

Sasha: Note: if kv_prefetch=true we must watch VRAM pressure. On smallgpu nodes KV resident size sometimes spikes >2GB and that will OOM the worker if combined with larger batches. Recommend also enabling `kv_resident_limit_mb=1800` for canary.

Kevin: Ran local with kv_prefetch=true + token_target=64 + kv_resident_limit_mb=1800. Observed p99 drop ~8% and p99.9 drop ~12%, throughput -4%. No OOM in 12h soak.

Maria: OK plan: Jon -> kick canary tonight with those overrides + kv_resident_limit_mb=1800. Collect 24h of metrics, especially p99.9, kernel selection histogram, KV hit rate. If regression resolves, schedule staged rollout with rollback knob.

Jon: On it. Will post results here once the canary finishes. /cc @Sasha @Kevin

Sasha: Also let's add a lightweight profiler hook to capture kernel_selector decisions during the canary (only sample 1/100 requests) so we can see whether we regain preferred kernels.

Maria: Good call. I'll open a tiny PR to add sampling and a dashboard panel. Thanks all :thumbsup:
